speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: asked the Minister for National Development whether the Home Improvement Programme can be extended to flats built after 1986 when they reach 30 years.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: First, in the older part of Nee Soon South, I have half of the total of HDB flats there which are built in 1985/1986 and the other half built in 1987/1988.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, very often, residents would ask me "为 什 么 对 面 有, 我 们 没 有?", and the flats are reaching 30 years old.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: When you first announced those that were selected, we were talking about flats of 30 years.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, I would like to ask the Minister whether he can get the funding and announce the next batch so that they will know that they will have it, rather than keep comparing with the blocks across the street.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Page: 13 Second, after doing these few batches of HIP, would there be modifications in the design?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The feedback from some of those early batches is that "Before HIP, I do not have music during the rainy days.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Now, after HIP, I always hear 'tick tock, tick tock'." That means some design modification is required.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I think the clothes drying poles also need modification.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will, indeed, take into consideration, should there be a new scheme, all the feedback from residents and see how future upgrading can be improved.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: On the budget, this is something that we are studying.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is something that we would have to think very carefully about and consider.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Certainly, from a Ministry of National Development point of view, I will be very happy to support this and I will want all our older towns to be upgraded as soon as possible.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: From a Ministry of Finance (MOF) perspective – and perhaps here I wear my other hat now – I have to say we will have to consider this very carefully and study it to make sure that budget availability is sustainable.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: From the MOF point of view, I think it is good to push out more HIP.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Because of the economic downturn, a lot of contractors out there are hungry for jobs, you will get value-for-money.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: I would just like to ask a supplementary question: if the programme cannot be extended in its totality, with regard to the clothes hanging facility, that is because of an ageing population causing quite a lot of challenges for the older flats.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: For the residents to be able to actually use those contraptions now, it is challenging and poses a safety issue as well.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Can consideration be given at least to look at upgrading and modifying that for residents?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As part of these major upgrading programmes, we have various other smaller refinement, fine-tuning, upgrading schemes that are also in place.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will always take into consideration feedback, like the ones that have been expressed about the hanging of clothes, and we will see what we can do in future rounds of upgrading to see how these can be taken into consideration.
